title: LASH terminal trench, Duncan's Taylor series example

meta.title: LASH terminal trench, Duncan's Taylor series example
meta.notes: Underwater trench in San Francisco Bay Mud: Su = 100 psf at el. −20 ft increasing 9.8 psf/ft, γ = 100 pcf, water at el. 0. Duncan's surface as a circle, Spencer; σγ = 3.3 pcf and σ of the Su gradient 1.2 psf/ft (a commercial program's Table 29.2). Converted to SI.

source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V023 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Above el. −20 ft cSlope extrapolates Su linearly (below 100 psf); program D keeps 100 psf there (F = 1.146, β = 0.947 when cSlope does the same). Duncan's F is 1.17; commercial program A's Latin hypercube Monte Carlo gives Pf = 14 % with a rate-only σ.

commercial program A analyses Duncan's non-circular surface (Spencer 1.157, GLE 1.160, Janbu corrected 1.168, Janbu 1.127). Its polyline, digitised from its fig. 29.2 (300 dpi, calibrated on the printed endpoints (137.767, −120.245) and (350.168, −7.761)), gives in cSlope Spencer 1.174, M-P 1.177, Janbu corrected 1.186, Janbu 1.149: +1.4 to +1.9 % on every method, so the surface's position, not the mechanics. Its interior vertices 2 ft higher give +2.7 %, 2 ft lower −2.2 % (Su grows with depth). Duncan (2000) fig. 4 is a sketch with an elevation axis only; read with the 0.875:1 slopes as scale, its estimated failure surface lies within 2–3 ft of the program's polyline, the drawing's precision, so the 1.5 % cannot be settled from the source. Fig. 2(b) confirms Su = 100 psf at el. −20 ft and 9.8 psf/ft.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
agua embalsada: la piezométrica pasa sobre el terreno; ogs la incluye en todas las versiones, con su peso y su empuje horizontal y sin sismo (F5.3); cSlope la carga con `followBoundary: false`.
